newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's king says he fears ASEAN membership.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's king says he fears ASEAN membership.

text.p: King Norodom Sihanouk has expressed strong reservations about Cambodia joining the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), fearing disastrous economic and social costs.

Sihanouk's views, released in a palace release on Thursday, are a strong departure from those of his government, which has embraced the prospect of ASEAN and expressed hopes that it can win entry in the regional grouping soon.
Cambodia has observer status in the regional bloc but hopes to become a member in July alongside Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
ASEAN has said Cambodia, Laos and Burma will join simultaneously.
Sihanouk said he shared the views expressed in a memorandum attached to the palace release.

The memorandum, whose author was not named, said membership of ASEAN would entail expense, eradicate duty revenues of about $250 million, flood the country with imports, stunt local economic growth and herald unchecked immigration at a time when Cambodia was still weak.
Sihanouk said Cambodia's only advantage in joining would be to protect its land and sea borders from larger neighbours, which include Thailand and Vietnam.
"One must hope ... that in entering ASEAN, Cambodia will gain something -- its return to the legitimate land and maritime borders of the 1950s and 1960s," Sihanouk said.

But once the country joined, he said, Cambodians "will not fail to be very disagreeably surprised to see that they and their country will suffer serious losses instead of the fabulous gains their leaders, ministers and other Khmer ASEANists have made sparkle in their eyes".
The king said foreigners would flood to the country not to help, but to compete against disadvantaged locals.
Sihanouk has long opposed Cambodia joining regional bodies and promoted a policy of non-alignment and neutrality.
